SMTO-EXE-0017 — Your recovery choice no longer matches the blocked step

GUID: 0147767a-2b85-49f5-a0f5-703c55e4e661
Slug: resource-reconciliation-invalid-correlation
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • Your choice was meant for a blocked command that SMTO can no longer match up. That command may already have been cancelled or started, or the blocking job is gone. Your choice wasn't applied.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page and open the task again. The task has moved on, and the reloaded page shows what is actually blocked now.
  2. If a recovery card still appears in the task, make your choice again on that card. The new card refers to the command that is blocked now, so your choice can be matched to it.
  3. If no card appears, check whether the task was stopped or has continued on its own. A stopped or already-started command no longer needs a recovery choice.

What success looks like

  • The task continues, or a fresh recovery card accepts your choice.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep resending the old choice; it refers to a step that no longer matches.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway rejected the reconciliation because the request did not correlate with a retained source job (wrong or missing run or event ID, source already executed or cancelled, no blocking jobs, or blocker outside the source's blocking set).

What this means

  • Reconciliation could not match a retained source job, owning run/event or resource scope, or found that the source had executed, been cancelled or lacked the expected blockers. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Reconciliation could not match a retained source job, owning run/event or resource scope, or found that the source had executed, been cancelled or lacked the expected blockers.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect source operation, run, decision event, cancellation state and blocker scope; do not substitute a new PID or unrelated job.

How to fix it

  • Compare the request's run ID, event ID and source_operation_id with the Gateway job record (run_id, executed, remote_effect_possible, cancellation_state, blocking_job_ids, resource_scope). Refresh the run's recovery projection and submit against the current blocked operation; if the source already executed or was cancelled, no reconciliation is needed.
  • Refresh the blocker and submit the action using current operation and resource references.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Current authoritative correlation checks pass for the same blocked operation and resource.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
